text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of your code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make the code cleaner and easier to read, not to add new features. By renaming unclear variables, breaking long functions into smaller ones, and removing duplicated logic, you make the code more understandable for yourself and other developers. This practice also helps reduce technical debt—the extra work caused by taking shortcuts in the past. While refactoring takes time, it pays off in the long run, as well-structured code is simpler to maintain, test, and extend.
